chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever sneezes, then places his hand upon the bridge of his nose, then says: 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, abundant praise as He is worthy of it, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and his Progeny and grant him peace,' a bird smaller than a locust and larger than a fly will emerge from his left nostril, until it travels beneath the Throne, seeking forgiveness for him from Allah until the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting the specific supplication after sneezing in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this unique narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the physical act of sneezing to a metaphysical reward, where a bird emerges from the left nostril to intercede for the believer. This imagery underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual significance of daily bodily functions, transforming mundane actions into opportunities for continuous divine forgiveness until the Day of Judgment.
